Marissa / team — uploaded a draft RFI answer (RFI_response_draft.docx) and a quick NIST mapping (NIST_mapping.xlsx). Highlights below (pull from doc for the response):

NIST AI RMF mapping (summary):
- Identify: Asset inventory for models (model registry with versioning; owner, training dataset lineage).
- Protect: Role-based access controls, KMS integration for keys, TLS in transit, optional HSM for private deployments.
- Detect: Real-time inference telemetry, anomaly detectors for latency/distribution shifts, model drift metrics on embeddings & token distributions.
- Respond: Automated routing to fallback model variant, incident playbooks, and customer-notification templates.
- Recover: Version rollback, immutable model artifacts in object storage, and post-incident evaluation logs.

Evaluation & regression approach:
- Continuous evals: We run nightly synthetic and seeded evals (prompt suites + performance and safety checks) against pinned baseline metrics.
- Dataset/versioning: Training and eval datasets are hashed & tracked in the model registry; we keep a snapshot per release.
- Regression detection: Threshold-based alerts for metric regression (accuracy/ROUGE/QA F1 as applicable), plus scorecard alerts tied to specific prompt sets.
- Canary rollouts: Gradual traffic ramp with canary metric gates; automatic rollback on negative regressions.
- Auditability: Every eval run is stored with metadata (model_version, commit, eval_suite_id) accessible via the Console.

Attachments included: RFI_response_draft.docx, NIST_mapping.xlsx.

I left some TODOs (EU Act phrasing, SOC2 reference) for Lauren/Neha.

Team — quick legal notes to incorporate into the response draft:

1) EU AI Act positioning:
- For our hosted API: treat Redwood as a system provider offering a general-purpose foundation. Most standard API usage is not "high-risk" under the current draft — however, customers can build high-risk systems on top of our API; in those cases, responsibility for the downstream classification typically sits with the deployer/customer.
- For Dedicated/Private: we provide customer-managed deployment options (VPC/on-prem) and data-flow controls; include explicit language that customers retain control of inputs/outputs and are responsible for controllers' obligations where they configure the model for regulated use.
- DPIA: we can provide a DPIA template and support materials; we do not perform DPIAs for customer-specific applications but will provide required technical information to assist customers.

2) Sensitive uses / obligations:
- Recommend we include a list of prohibited use-cases (e.g., automated credit denials without human review) and a statement about escalation for suspected misuse.

3) Evidence & attestation:
- Provide SOC 2 summary (not full report in first pass). Note that FedRAMP/ISO27001 are not currently available; if that's a blocking requirement, we should flag for procurement.

Hi James / BlueHarbor Security team —

Thanks for the opportunity to respond. Attached is our consolidated RFI response and supporting artifacts. Executive summary below:

1) NIST AI RMF alignment: We map our controls and operational practices to the five NIST functions (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover). For example, our model registry and asset inventory map to "Identify," KMS/HSM and RBAC map to "Protect," and our telemetry and anomaly detectors map to "Detect." See NIST_mapping.xlsx for the full matrix.

2) EU AI Act positioning: For Redwood's hosted API we act as a provider of general-purpose inference services. Most standard API use-cases are not classified as "high-risk" by default; customers building regulated systems are responsible for downstream obligations. For customers requiring stronger assurances, Redwood offers Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and technical controls (data isolation, customer-managed keys) to help meet deployer/controller responsibilities. We can provide a DPIA template and technical appendices to assist your teams.

3) Evaluation & regression approach: Redwood runs continuous evaluation suites (nightly synthetic and customer-seeded tests), maintains hashed dataset/versioning in the model registry, and triggers regression alerts tied to gates used in canary rollouts. Audit trails for eval runs and model promotions are available in the Console and included in the attached documentation.

4) Evidence & attestations: SOC 2 summary attached; we also included model cards for the public models we serve and a mapping spreadsheet. Full SOC 2 report or additional compliance attestations can be provided under NDA / on an as-requested basis.

Attachments: BlueHarbor_RFI_Response_20260305.pdf, SOC2_summary.pdf, NIST_mapping.xlsx
